accuracy.evidence: Matches CCSS K.OA.5 fluent add/subtract within 5; five-frame and subitising language match NCETM early number guidance; totals and take-aways stay in 0–5 except where past-5 is labelled as outside the set.

misconceptions.evidence: Challenge and adult text target sticking digits (2+3→23), finger-counting instead of recall, treating 3+3=6 as within 5, swapping add/subtract, and echoing a visible number instead of the hidden part.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab is built around within-5 fluency: flash subitising, five-frame, hide-and-say on 5, race-the-fingers, all pairs for 4 — not reusable for bonds-to-10 or teen structure without rewriting the mechanism.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner discovers totals from dots and empty five-frame spaces, then confirms with equations; race and build steps require producing facts, not only reading them.

predictions.evidence: Predictions offer tempting wrong options (23, echoing 2, 'always count fingers', 5−5) that the following task disproves on the canvas.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names stick, sub, add, echo, zero, five, fingers, onlyadd, force — each tied to a specific slip on that item.

readability.evidence: Kid lines are short concrete sentences for ages 5–6; adult names curriculum codes and mistakes without jargon piles.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid/adult sentence teaches a fact, a representation, or a mistake; no journey/explore/delve phrasing.

mobile.evidence: Big lbtn targets, five-frame drag, number pads; young class and tall shell ratio match other 5–6 labs.

accessibility.evidence: All actions have buttons as well as drag; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: CCSS K.OA.5 Fluently add and subtract within 5
NCETM Early Number Sense / five-frames guidance
UK National Curriculum 2013 Mathematics Year 1: represent and use number bonds and related subtraction facts within 10
